concept.title: Mapping rules
concept.shortdesc: A mapping rule rewrites one kind of DITA element into DITA that converts cleanly, before conversion. Rules are small XSLT templates that a writer reviews and approves.

conbody.p: Some elements have no Markdown equivalent. A choicetable, for example, can become a simpletable with the same rows and ID. A rule records what it matches, what it does, who proposed it, which run it came from, and who approved it.
Rules run on a working copy, never on your source, and the checks still compare against the untouched source. A rule can only make a topic pass by making the migrated page match the published one.
Because a model writes some rules, every rule is limited before it runs: XSLT templates only, no file or network access, no imports and no extension functions.
